answer: Operator Liability Ledger. Each identity's actions are cryptographically tied to a legal entity via signed deployment manifests; when duplicate behavioral fingerprints surface across wallets (shared timing nebula, identical call graphs), the ledger fines the operator's registered account and suspends all its identities. An attacker must forge distinct legal entities per clone, paying incorporation, compliance, and audit costs per identity—and a tundra of frozen collateral plus operator-level bans if caught.
